title: Recap the example or the task
statement: Whether a recap offered during independent practice should restate the worked example, signposted as the example, or describe the learner's current task is unsettled.
example: In one scan, 5 of 7 recaps in two lessons gave no sign that they described the worked example rather than the learner's own question.
detail: A cross-field scan of two Grade 3 lessons found every recap accurate to the worked example it summarised, but the hint's label gave a struggling child no sign that it was about a different character and place from the question on screen, so the child could take it for a hint about their own answer. The scan called this a labelling question, suggested signposting the recap as the example, and routed it for a ruling without changing anything. A later repair took the other route and replaced the carryover recaps in two lessons with summaries of the current task's own material.
against: The risk the scan named is predicted, not observed with a child (`grade3-reading/artifacts/signoff-packet/CROSS-FIELD-SCAN-2026-08-31.md`, lines 96-105), and another record keeps such recaps on the worked example's own material.

evidence.quote: A child who taps the hint mid-task, without holding the "watch me think" page in memory, will read "gloomy, miserable, strict" or "Lost Boys... gentle, lonely" while looking at a Neverland/Hook question and can easily mistake it for a hint about their OWN answer
This is a UX/labeling question (should the recap open with "On my London example, I..." or similar signposting)
(5 of 7 teacher_recap instances in the scanned lessons; L4/p22 and p22d already open with unambiguous topic framing or are place-agnostic)
Replaced carryover London/Lost Boys summaries with the current Neverland/Hook fit-word summaries.
